strengths: Well-motivated problem bridging BEV's spatial consistency with LLM's semantic richness, addressing genuine gap in autonomous driving
Rigorous representation study (Section 3) with multiple datasets (DriveLM, Ego3D) and VLMs showing convincing BEV advantages (46% MCQ accuracy improvement on cross-view reasoning)
Strong safety-critical evaluation emphasis on closed-loop metrics over open-loop, with meaningful improvements (29% NeuroNCAP score, 11.3% collision rate reduction)
Comprehensive ablations including VQA data types and token downsampling methods, with clear insights on what matters (behavior/planning > perception/prediction)
Thoughtful technical design: joint training with detection preserves spatial structure, frozen LLM is computationally efficient, coordinate conversion well-justified
Clear presentation with good visualizations and honest discussion of limitations in appendix
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: MLP projector alignment is standard (similar to LLaVA), distillation mechanism uses straightforward cross-entropy proxy, incremental over existing work
Significant generalization concerns: only BEVFormer/UniAD architecture tested (acknowledged 100h+ cost per variant), only nuScenes for distillation, limited VQA dataset (~300k hand-curated samples)
Dataset bias not fully addressed: filtering of DriveLM questions removes samples with objects outside BEV range, potentially introducing bias toward easy spatial reasoning scenarios
Unclear what semantic knowledge is actually learned: no visualization of distilled BEV features or interpretation of safety concepts captured; the semantic manifold concept is somewhat hand-wavy
Evaluation concerns: NeuroNCAP only ~5 detailed corner cases shown, high collision rates even for improved model (55%), lack of statistical significance testing, no error bars or confidence intervals

Comparison fairness issues: UniAD detection baseline conflates different tasks; IViT comparison has very different token counts/architectures; limited comparison with recent VLM-based driving methods (LMDrive, DriveVLM, VLM-AD)
Insufficient ablations: no frozen vs. fine-tuned LLM comparison, contribution of detection loss vs. VQA loss not isolated, coordinate conversion procedure not fully validated
Practical applicability limited: 100+ hour training on 8 A100 GPUs for single architecture/dataset, no inference cost analysis, unclear how well synthetic benchmark transfers to real-world deployment

Incomplete analysis: why does BEV MCQ accuracy remain only 67.44% on Ego3D (Table 3)? Why such small differences in 8B results (Table 2)? One clear failure case shown (Corner Case 5) with limited failure analysis

strengths: Well-motivated systematic representation study showing BEV tokens improve LLM cross-view spatial reasoning by 46% compared to perspective views, with strong evidence from multiple datasets (DriveLM, Ego3D)

Significant practical safety improvements in closed-loop autonomous driving evaluation (28.2% NeuroNCAP score improvement, 16.1% collision rate reduction) validated across two different end-to-end frameworks (UniAD, VAD)

Comprehensive experimental methodology with appropriate baselines (majority class, linear probe, detection head), proper uncertainty quantification (mean±std over 50 runs), and thorough ablations on token downsampling and VQA data types
Clear presentation with well-motivated problem formulation, good figures, and extensive supplementary materials enabling reproducibility
Appropriate focus on safety-critical evaluation through NeuroNCAP closed-loop benchmark, addressing important concerns for autonomous driving beyond standard open-loop metrics
Thoughtful contribution design showing both BEV advantages for LLM reasoning and practical benefits through semantic distillation framework
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—semantic distillation mechanism is straightforward (frozen LLM teacher + MLP projector), applying well-established VLM alignment techniques to BEV context rather than introducing new methods

Generality concerns severely limited by testing only on BEVFormer-based architectures (UniAD, VAD); authors defer testing alternative BEV encoders (BEVDet, BEVFusion, BEVerse) due to computational constraints, undermining broad applicability claims
Single VQA dataset (DriveLM-nuScenes) used for distillation; no evaluation on alternative driving VQA datasets, raising questions about generalization to other semantic supervision sources

Insufficient analysis of coordinate conversion from image-plane to ego-centric BEV frame; missing quantitative validation of conversion accuracy, data loss rates, and potential systematic biases affecting semantic distillation

Weak comparison with VLM-AD baseline (NeuroNCAP 2.02-2.07 vs BEVLM 3.05) raises concerns—was the VLM-AD implementation optimal? Recreation from 'original recipe' rather than official code makes it difficult to assess if the comparison is fair

Limited interpretability and analysis of learned semantics; lacks visualization of feature changes, probing experiments, or attention analysis to demonstrate what safety-related features are actually distilled from LLMs
Extremely high computational cost (~100 hours on 8 A100 GPUs for distillation + 115 hours E2E training) significantly limits reproducibility and practical adoption by broader community
Reliance on human-curated VQA data (DriveLM) for supervision; acknowledged limitation of 'human-labor-free distillation' deferred to future work reduces practical applicability
No systematic analysis of failure modes; Figure 7 shows BEVLM still crashes in challenging scenarios—unclear which scenario types remain problematic and where distillation provides least benefit

Question filtering may introduce bias; reducing DriveLM from full dataset to 3,609 questions based on spatial extent matching could bias toward well-represented scenarios, but no systematic analysis provided
